title.narrative: Lean Season Lifeline: Integrated Prevention and Treatment of acute malnutrition in Banki and Ngala.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn response to the lean season, FHI 360 proposes a targeted intervention to address acute malnutrition through an integrated approach combining facility-based treatment, community-level prevention, and psychosocial support. FHI 360 will strengthen the capacity of three existing Stabilization Centres (SCs) in Banki and Ngala to manage SAM with medical complications in children aged 0–59 months. This includes expanding bed capacity, providing essential pharmaceuticals, and deploying surge human resources. Caregivers will receive three balanced meals daily during admission. Upon discharge cash-for-transport stipends would be provided. To improve household dietary diversity and access to nutrient-dense foods, FHI 360 will implement the Cash Plus for Nutrition model—Resourcing Families for Better Nutrition (RF4BN)—alongside lifesaving nutrition interventions for children under five and pregnant/breastfeeding women and girls (PBWG). The intervention will target 700 vulnerable households enrolled in SCs, providing three monthly tranches of e-vouchers valued at ₦12,325 for U5 and ₦13,634 for PBWG, plus a ₦3,000 transport top-up. The voucher basket aligns with the CVA for North-East Nutrition Guideline and includes fresh items from the regional sentinel food list to address dietary gaps.ltbrgtThe SCs will receive referrals from FHI 360-supported Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) and other partners, including BoSPHCDB. Mortality audits will be conducted to uphold Sphere standards. FHI 360 will scale up active case findings and IMAM services in OTPs across both LGAs, supplying medical commodities for the treatment of common illnesses associated with SAM, and training health workers on IMAM and Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN). All SAM patients will receive hygiene kits on discharge from treatment. MIYCN counselling will be delivered at both facility and community levels to support optimal feeding practices.ltbrgtTo foster sustained behavior change, FHI 360 will establish 160 community-based support groups, each comprising 8–15 members, to facilitate Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) on MIYCN. Children aged 6–59 months will receive vitamin A supplementation, micronutrient powders, and deworming. Mothers and caregivers will be trained in family-led MUAC screening to enhance early detection and coverage.ltbrgtFHI 360 proposes to address the health-related underlying causes of Severe Acute Malnutrition. This health-focused initiative complements and strengthens the continuum of care by integrating clinical management of common childhood illnesses that exacerbate the burden of malnutrition. FHI 360 proposes to deploy mobile medical teams in Ngala and Banki to deliver essential primary health care servicess. The Mobile Medical teams will complement activities at the nutrition OTPs. The Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) for children under 5 will be implemented to enable early detection, effective treatment and prompt referral of common childhood illnesses at the community level.ltbrgtAt facility and community levels, FHI 360 will also conduct screening of children under five for malnutrition and facilitate referrals to appropriate nutrition services. These interventions directly contribute to the Health Cluster objective under the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP): provision of quality, lifesaving, integrated health services to affected populations including IDPs, returnees, host communities, and those in hard-to-reach areas. Capacity-building efforts will extend to health workers, with tailored training on IMCI and nutrition-focused topics. FHI 360 will integrate gender, protection, and disability considerations to ensure inclusive and equitable access to services for all vulnerable groupsltbrgtBy integrating health and nutrition, this proposal offers a holistic, evidence-based response to reduce morbidity and mortality, strengthen resilience, and restore dignity to communities impacted by conflict and displacement.ltbrgtlt/pgt
